{"people":[{"name":"Lucy","role":"Ecommerce director, champion","side":"customer"},{"name":"Martin","role":"CFO, final decision-maker (rep never met him)","side":"customer"},{"name":"unnamed","role":"Controller (prepared the one-pager rate comparison for Martin)","side":"customer"},{"name":"unnamed","role":"IT lead","side":"customer"},{"name":"Sam","role":"Account executive (rep)","side":"us"},{"name":"Farah","role":"Solutions engineer","side":"us"},{"name":"PMM","role":"Product marketer (interviewer)","side":"us"},{"name":"the bank","role":"Customer's bank, provider of incumbent Fiserv processing; came back with a sharper rate","side":"competitor"}],
"competitors":["Fiserv (through the customer's bank)"],
"incumbent":"Fiserv through their bank",
"evidence":[
{"id":"E1","turn":2,"excerpt":"Their ecommerce director, Lucy, came inbound. Orders failing at checkout.","label":"fact","speaker":"rep","paraphrase":false,"topics":["trigger"],"note":"Inbound evaluation triggered by checkout failures."},
{"id":"E2","turn":2,"excerpt":"She said about one in twelve online orders was failing at the payment step, and it was worse on the big baskets.","label":"fact","speaker":"Lucy (relayed by rep)","paraphrase":true,"topics":["trigger","language"],"note":"Quantified pain from the customer, concentrated on large orders."},
{"id":"E3","turn":4,"excerpt":"Her number. Off their own dashboard.","label":"fact","speaker":"rep","paraphrase":false,"topics":["trigger"],"note":"The 1-in-12 figure comes from the customer's own data, not ours."},
{"id":"E4","turn":2,"excerpt":"Customers would call in annoyed, or just not come back.","label":"opinion","speaker":"rep","paraphrase":true,"topics":["trigger"],"note":"Downstream cost of failures; source unclear, not quoted."},
{"id":"E5","turn":2,"excerpt":"she couldn't get a straight answer from the processor on why.","label":"fact","speaker":"Lucy (relayed by rep)","paraphrase":true,"topics":["trigger","competitor"],"note":"Incumbent weakness: no explanation of declines."},
{"id":"E6","turn":6,"excerpt":"The CFO, Martin. Lucy was the champion, she wanted it, IT was fine with it. Martin said no.","label":"fact","speaker":"rep","paraphrase":false,"topics":["decider","outcome"],"note":"Decider was the CFO, not the champion."},
{"id":"E7","turn":6,"excerpt":"Lucy told me. I never met him.","label":"fact","speaker":"rep","paraphrase":false,"topics":["decider"],"note":"Rep never had access to the decider; all secondhand."},
{"id":"E8","turn":8,"excerpt":"Lucy said he doesn't take vendor meetings and she'd carry it.","label":"fact","speaker":"Lucy (relayed by rep)","paraphrase":true,"topics":["decider"],"note":"Champion carried the case to the CFO alone."},
{"id":"E9","turn":10,"excerpt":"They were on Fiserv through their bank, had been forever.","label":"fact","speaker":"rep","paraphrase":false,"topics":["competitor"],"note":"Long-standing incumbent bundled with the bank."},
{"id":"E10","turn":10,"excerpt":"when the bank heard, they came back and sharpened the rate.","label":"fact","speaker":"Lucy (relayed by rep)","paraphrase":true,"topics":["competitor"],"note":"Incumbent's counter-move was a price cut, reported by the customer."},
{"id":"E11","turn":10,"excerpt":"No new product, nothing. Just a better rate.","label":"opinion","speaker":"rep","paraphrase":false,"topics":["competitor"],"note":"Rep's characterization of the competitor response."},
{"id":"E12","turn":12,"excerpt":"Up to then Lucy was asking about declines. Why big orders fail, what we'd do about it.","label":"fact","speaker":"rep","paraphrase":false,"topics":["competitor","message"],"note":"Customer questions were about declines before the bank's counter."},
{"id":"E13","turn":12,"excerpt":"After the bank came back, every email was the rate. Can you do better on the rate.","label":"fact","speaker":"rep","paraphrase":false,"topics":["competitor","decided"],"note":"Observable shift from value to price after the incumbent's counter."},
{"id":"E14","turn":14,"excerpt":"Lucy loved the checkout. And the decline piece.","label":"opinion","speaker":"rep","paraphrase":false,"topics":["message"],"note":"Rep's read of what resonated with the champion."},
{"id":"E15","turn":14,"excerpt":"When our solutions engineer, Farah, explained why big-ticket orders get knocked back and what we do about it, Lucy was nodding the whole way.","label":"fact","speaker":"rep","paraphrase":false,"topics":["message","language"],"note":"Observed reaction to the decline explanation."},
{"id":"E16","turn":14,"excerpt":"Silence, honestly, nothing bombed. It was a good cycle. We lost on price.","label":"opinion","speaker":"rep","paraphrase":false,"topics":["message","outcome"],"note":"Rep attributes the loss to price; claims no message failed."},
{"id":"E17","turn":16,"excerpt":"he's not going to pay more for the same thing.","label":"quote","speaker":"Lucy","paraphrase":false,"topics":["decided","language","outcome"],"note":"Moment of loss; the CFO saw no differentiation."},
{"id":"E18","turn":16,"excerpt":"Right before that she'd been telling me it was a formality.","label":"fact","speaker":"rep","paraphrase":false,"topics":["decided","decider"],"note":"Champion overestimated her ability to carry the CFO."},
{"id":"E19","turn":18,"excerpt":"The controller did a one-pager for Martin. Our rate, their rate, side by side.","label":"fact","speaker":"rep","paraphrase":false,"topics":["decider","decided"],"note":"The decision artifact was a rate-only comparison built by the customer."},
{"id":"E20","turn":20,"excerpt":"Yeah. The per-transaction number.","label":"fact","speaker":"rep","paraphrase":false,"topics":["decided"],"note":"Only the per-transaction rate was compared."},
{"id":"E21","turn":20,"excerpt":"they pay a gateway fee on top, and they've got a person who does nothing but chargebacks.","label":"opinion","speaker":"rep","paraphrase":false,"topics":["gaps"],"note":"Hidden incumbent costs the rep knew about but were never put in front of the CFO."},
{"id":"E22","turn":20,"excerpt":"But that's not on the statement line, so it wasn't on the page.","label":"fact","speaker":"rep","paraphrase":false,"topics":["gaps","decided"],"note":"Total cost was missing from the decision page."},
{"id":"E23","turn":22,"excerpt":"Our quote.","label":"fact","speaker":"rep","paraphrase":false,"topics":["gaps"],"note":"Our only input on the decision page was price."},
{"id":"E24","turn":24,"excerpt":"Martin and the controller. I wasn't in the room. Lucy presented it.","label":"fact","speaker":"rep","paraphrase":false,"topics":["decider"],"note":"No one from our side was present at the decision."},
{"id":"E25","turn":24,"excerpt":"Why would I pay more for the same thing.","label":"quote","speaker":"Martin (relayed secondhand via Lucy)","paraphrase":false,"topics":["decided","language"],"note":"Decider's framing: parity product, higher price."},
{"id":"E26","turn":26,"excerpt":"Which it isn't. But that's what he said.","label":"opinion","speaker":"rep","paraphrase":false,"topics":["language","message"],"note":"Rep disputes the 'same thing' perception but did not counter it."},
{"id":"E27","turn":28,"excerpt":"We showed the uplift slide. The average improvement in acceptance.","label":"fact","speaker":"rep","paraphrase":false,"topics":["message","gaps"],"note":"Value was shown generically, not specific to Fernbrook."},
{"id":"E28","turn":28,"excerpt":"Lucy got it.","label":"opinion","speaker":"rep","paraphrase":false,"topics":["message"],"note":"The value landed with the champion, not the decider."},
{"id":"E29","turn":30,"excerpt":"Not in a doc, no.","label":"fact","speaker":"rep","paraphrase":false,"topics":["gaps"],"note":"No Fernbrook-specific value figure was ever produced."},
{"id":"E30","turn":30,"excerpt":"Farah offered to run their declines. She wanted a three-month export so she could show what the failed orders were worth.","label":"fact","speaker":"rep","paraphrase":false,"topics":["gaps"],"note":"The SE offered a quantified business case; it never happened."},
{"id":"E31","turn":30,"excerpt":"it was the last two weeks of the quarter, and I didn't want to slow things down.","label":"fact","speaker":"rep","paraphrase":false,"topics":["gaps"],"note":"Quarter-end pressure led the rep to skip the value analysis."},
{"id":"E32","turn":30,"excerpt":"Lucy was sold. I didn't think we needed it.","label":"opinion","speaker":"rep","paraphrase":false,"topics":["gaps","decider"],"note":"Rep sold to the champion, not the decider."},
{"id":"E33","turn":32,"excerpt":"Nothing from us.","label":"fact","speaker":"rep","paraphrase":false,"topics":["gaps"],"note":"The CFO had no cost-of-failure data from us."},
{"id":"E34","turn":32,"excerpt":"I assume Lucy told him.","label":"opinion","speaker":"rep","paraphrase":false,"topics":["gaps","decider"],"note":"Unverified assumption about what reached the decider."},
{"id":"E35","turn":34,"excerpt":"Yes. Probably.","label":"opinion","speaker":"rep","paraphrase":false,"topics":["outcome"],"note":"Hedged claim that a price match would have won."},
{"id":"E36","turn":34,"excerpt":"their IT lead was a bit nervous about moving before spring, that's their whole year.","label":"opinion","speaker":"rep","paraphrase":false,"topics":["decided","outcome"],"note":"A second, non-price obstacle: migration risk before peak season."},
{"id":"E37","turn":34,"excerpt":"He'd said he'd do it if finance approved.","label":"fact","speaker":"IT lead (relayed by rep)","paraphrase":true,"topics":["decider"],"note":"IT's approval was conditional on finance."},
{"id":"E38","turn":34,"excerpt":"So maybe not only the rate. But the rate is what killed it.","label":"opinion","speaker":"rep","paraphrase":false,"topics":["outcome"],"note":"Rep self-corrects, then reverts to price."},
{"id":"E39","turn":36,"excerpt":"Lucy asked once if we had something she could hand Martin. Like a one-page business case.","label":"fact","speaker":"Lucy (relayed by rep)","paraphrase":true,"topics":["gaps"],"note":"Explicit ask from the champion for CFO-ready material."},
{"id":"E40","turn":36,"excerpt":"I sent her the deck and the pricing proposal.","label":"fact","speaker":"rep","paraphrase":false,"topics":["gaps"],"note":"The business-case request was answered with generic material."},
{"id":"E41","turn":38,"excerpt":"The customer stories. The average uplift.","label":"fact","speaker":"rep","paraphrase":false,"topics":["gaps","message"],"note":"The deck's 'business case' was generic, not Fernbrook's numbers."},
{"id":"E42","turn":40,"excerpt":"orders dying at the last step.","label":"quote","speaker":"Lucy","paraphrase":false,"topics":["language"],"note":"Customer's words for declines."},
{"id":"E43","turn":40,"excerpt":"the big baskets.","label":"quote","speaker":"Lucy","paraphrase":false,"topics":["language"],"note":"Customer's words for big-ticket orders."},
{"id":"E44","turn":40,"excerpt":"we do all the work to get someone to buy a four-thousand-dollar greenhouse and then the card says no.","label":"quote","speaker":"Lucy","paraphrase":false,"topics":["language","trigger"],"note":"Vivid customer framing of the pain, with an order value."},
{"id":"E45","turn":42,"excerpt":"If we'd had more room on the rate, we win this.","label":"opinion","speaker":"rep","paraphrase":false,"topics":["outcome"],"note":"Rep's lesson is price only, despite the value gaps described."}
],
"contradictions":[
{"evidence":["E16","E38","E45"],"what":"Rep says the deal was lost on price, then concedes 'maybe not only the rate', then reverts to 'we win this' with more room on the rate."},
{"evidence":["E35","E36"],"what":"Rep says a price match would have won ('Yes. Probably.'), then describes IT nervousness about moving before spring and the CFO still seeing 'same rate, so why move'."},
{"evidence":["E16","E17","E25"],"what":"Rep says 'nothing bombed', but the decider concluded we were 'the same thing', so the differentiation message failed with him."},
{"evidence":["E28","E32","E39"],"what":"Rep says Lucy 'got it' and 'was sold', yet Lucy asked for something to hand Martin and never got a business case."},
{"evidence":["E18","E6","E17"],"what":"Lucy said approval was 'a formality' right before the CFO said no."},
{"evidence":["E29","E41"],"what":"Rep admits there was no Fernbrook value figure, but presents customer stories and average uplift as the business case in the deck."},
{"evidence":["E17","E25"],"what":"Rep says Martin's words are 'what I told you', but the two versions differ: 'he's not going to pay more for the same thing' vs 'Why would I pay more for the same thing'."}
],
"dodges":[
{"question":"Which part of our pitch got a reaction, and which got silence?","turn":14,"what":"Answered 'nothing bombed' and pivoted to price, ignoring that the value message never reached or convinced the decider."},
{"question":"Did we put a figure on the value they'd get?","turn":28,"what":"Answered with the generic uplift slide; admitted only when pressed that there was no Fernbrook figure."},
{"question":"So what did Martin have in front of him about what one in twelve orders was costing?","turn":32,"what":"Hesitated, said 'Nothing from us', then deflected with an assumption that Lucy told him."},
{"question":"If we had matched the price, would we have won?","turn":34,"what":"Hedged yes, listed non-price obstacles, then reasserted that the rate killed it."},
{"question":"Was there a business case in the deck?","turn":38,"what":"Did not answer yes or no; named customer stories and average uplift."},
{"question":"If you ran it again?","turn":42,"what":"Answered only about price room, skipping the value analysis and the business case he had just described as missing."}
],
"skipped":[],
"language_pairs":[
{"theirs":"orders dying at the last step","ours":"declines / improvement in acceptance","evidence":["E42","E12","E27"]},
{"theirs":"the big baskets","ours":"big-ticket orders","evidence":["E43","E15"]},
{"theirs":"the card says no","ours":"knocked back / declines","evidence":["E44","E15"]},
{"theirs":"the same thing","ours":"uplift / average improvement in acceptance","evidence":["E25","E27"]},
{"theirs":"a one-page business case","ours":"the deck and the pricing proposal","evidence":["E39","E40"]}
],
"outcome_signals":[
{"evidence":["E6","E17","E25"],"what":"Lost: the CFO said no because he saw no reason to pay more for 'the same thing'."},
{"evidence":["E10","E13","E19"],"what":"The customer stayed with the incumbent bank/Fiserv after the bank sharpened its rate; the decision was made on a rate-only comparison."},
{"evidence":["E16","E45"],"what":"Rep frames the loss as price."},
{"evidence":["E36","E38","E29","E33"],"what":"Other factors: IT's pre-spring migration risk, and no quantified value was put in front of the decider."},
{"evidence":["E6"],"what":"No indication that any part of the business moved; the whole deal was lost."}
]}

contradictions.what: Rep says the deal was lost on price, then concedes 'maybe not only the rate', then reverts to 'we win this' with more room on the rate.
Rep says a price match would have won ('Yes. Probably.'), then describes IT nervousness about moving before spring and the CFO still seeing 'same rate, so why move'.
Rep says 'nothing bombed', but the decider concluded we were 'the same thing', so the differentiation message failed with him.
Rep says Lucy 'got it' and 'was sold', yet Lucy asked for something to hand Martin and never got a business case.
Lucy said approval was 'a formality' right before the CFO said no.
Rep admits there was no Fernbrook value figure, but presents customer stories and average uplift as the business case in the deck.
Rep says Martin's words are 'what I told you', but the two versions differ: 'he's not going to pay more for the same thing' vs 'Why would I pay more for the same thing'.

dodges.question: Which part of our pitch got a reaction, and which got silence?
dodges.what: Answered 'nothing bombed' and pivoted to price, ignoring that the value message never reached or convinced the decider.

dodges.question: Did we put a figure on the value they'd get?
dodges.what: Answered with the generic uplift slide; admitted only when pressed that there was no Fernbrook figure.

dodges.question: So what did Martin have in front of him about what one in twelve orders was costing?
dodges.what: Hesitated, said 'Nothing from us', then deflected with an assumption that Lucy told him.

dodges.question: If we had matched the price, would we have won?
dodges.what: Hedged yes, listed non-price obstacles, then reasserted that the rate killed it.

dodges.question: Was there a business case in the deck?
dodges.what: Did not answer yes or no; named customer stories and average uplift.

dodges.question: If you ran it again?
dodges.what: Answered only about price room, skipping the value analysis and the business case he had just described as missing.

outcome_signals.what: Lost: the CFO said no because he saw no reason to pay more for 'the same thing'.
The customer stayed with the incumbent bank/Fiserv after the bank sharpened its rate; the decision was made on a rate-only comparison.
Rep frames the loss as price.
Other factors: IT's pre-spring migration risk, and no quantified value was put in front of the decider.
No indication that any part of the business moved; the whole deal was lost.
